_why_overrides: **Corrected 2026-09-08, and the correction is the point of this note.** The list below used
to be `["workbench-base"]` alone, on a measurement recorded as: "every one of BoingBag
3.9-1's 210 files sits at a path the base AmigaOS 3.9 recipe's `workbench-base` component
already writes - 100%, not merely 'some'". That was a claim about the *media*, and the
list has to be a claim about the **tree**: `distribution.json` records which component
actually placed each file, and AmigaOS 3.9's own recipe splits the Workbench across
`workbench-base` (the 3.5 half) and `workbench-39` (the 3.9 half). The first real host
placement, against the owner's own tree, refused with:
'boingbag-39-1' would write over 122 file(s) it never declared it may replace:
C/WBInfo, C/StringSnip, C/SetPatch, C/SetVNC, C/LoadMonDrvs, and 117 more
Counted against that tree's own manifest (2026-09-08): of this payload's 210 files, **122**
are recorded to `workbench-39`, **24** to `workbench-base`, and 64 are not in the tree at
all (new files, which overwrite nothing). So both are named, and the old note's 100% was
right about the disc and wrong about the tree - which is exactly the difference `overrides`
The original note is kept below, because the reason `overrides` may not simply be left
empty is still the reason it may not be:
_why_overrides_workbench_base: Fix round 1 (Task 4 review). The first version of this file shipped
`overrides: []`, reasoned from the wrong scope: every rule below is
`subtree`, and `no_two_components_claim_one_destination_without_declaring_it`
only polices `file` rules, so nothing here was ever a *rule-level*
collision needing a declaration. But `overrides` is not read by that test
alone — a later stage reads it at the *file* level, to tell a BoingBag
deliberately replacing a file from `declared_by_the_owner_component` from
a genuine surprise. Measured directly against the owner's real media
(Task 4 review): every one of BoingBag 3.9-1's 210 files sits at a path
the base AmigaOS 3.9 recipe's `workbench-base` component already writes —
100%, not merely 'some'. Leaving `overrides` empty made that whole
measured fact invisible to whatever reads it, which is worse than not
declaring anything: a constant `declared: false` on every one of a
BoingBag's rows tells a reader nothing, which is exactly the noise this
field exists to separate a real surprise from (spec §3).
`recipe.rs`'s `every_override_names_a_component_that_exists` originally
could not resolve this anyway: it checked `recipe.component(over)` against
the one-component pseudo-`Recipe` `shipped_recipes()` built for a package,
which never contains `workbench-base` — a different recipe's component
entirely. Fixed there (Task 4 review) by resolving `over` against the
union of every shipped id, releases and packages together, rather than
one recipe's own list — see `all_shipped_component_ids` in `recipe.rs`.
name: BoingBag 3.9-1
_why_releases: ART-209. A BoingBag is an AmigaOS 3.9 archive and there is no such thing
as a BoingBag for 3.2 — 3.2's own updates arrive as a release component
(`Update3.2.1` in amigaos-3.2.json), not as a package. Until this field
existed nothing could say so, and the owner choosing AmigaOS 3.2 was
offered BoingBags on the screen below the component checklist.
3.9 only, and not '3.9 and anything later': ART ships two recipes and a
third would be a new JSON file, at which point whether these apply to it
is a question somebody has to answer by looking, not a default.
_why_no_distinguished_by: ART-167 gave a package a second identity fact for archives whose
top-level directory is shared. This one's is not: across all 44 `.lha`
archives in the owner's package folder, exactly one carries
`LocaleUpdate` is claimed by eight and `BoingBag3.9-2` by two.
So no `distinguished_by` is declared, deliberately. A condition that
separates nothing cannot help, and it can hurt: a user whose own copy
is a repack without the exact inner path named here would be told the
archive is missing when it is not. Spec §89's rule about not
claiming more than is true cuts this way too.
_why_payload_password: ART-166, and the whole of its history, because a wrong elimination left standing costs
more than none.
**What was measured (2026-08-25, three independent ways: ART's own reader, 7-Zip 26.02,
the raw general-purpose flag word 0x0003 with bit 0 set).** The `AmigaOS-Update` member
named above is a ZIP whose every entry is ZipCrypto-encrypted - 233 of 233 entries in
3.9-1's payload, 147 of 147 in 3.9-2's. That measurement was and remains correct.
**What was concluded from it, twice, and was wrong.** This file used to carry
`host_placement_block: "encrypted-payload"`, on the reasoning that the key belongs to the
package's own `Updater` and that every established distribution builder runs that Updater
inside an emulator. The second half was never checked against the builders that had since
appeared. **Emu68 Hatcher** and **Emu68-Imager** - both MIT, both building AmigaOS 3.9 for
the same hardware ART targets - do exactly what this file said nobody does: they open the
payload with the key they publish in their own source and copy the files onto the tree
(`src/main/python/emu68hatcher/builder/staging/boingbag.py`, read whole on 2026-09-08).
**The owner's decision, 2026-09-08, in their own words:** "inatla BoingBag'i Windows
uzerinden yerlestirmedin; diger proje yapiyor bu isi, bu yuzden is kilitlendi" /
"avukatlik yapma, muhendisiz biz". It reverses the 2026-08-19 ruling. ART places BoingBag
1 and 2 from the host, the way those two projects do.
**The key below is Emu68 Hatcher's**, `93ABDF11`, attributed in
THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md with the file it comes from. Verified against the owner's own
`BoingBag39-1 (1).lha` on 2026-09-08 with Python's `zipfile`: 233 of 233 entries read
clean, and `C/WBRun` and `Libs/xadmaster.library` both begin `000003F3`, the AmigaOS hunk
header - so the bytes are real programs and not noise that happened to decrypt.
**The `amiga_installer` block was removed on 2026-09-08**, one round after the reversal
above. It declared the emulator route for this package - `C/Updater`, its `minimum_version`,
its UAE overlay, the AmigaOS 3.9 CD it verifies, its ten `post_install` protection bits -
and every one of those facts is now either unused or restated below as host-side data:
`post_place` carries the same ten bits, and the payload the Updater used to decrypt is
opened by `payload_password` above. Keeping a second route nothing takes would have been
ART claiming an install path it no longer runs (section 89). The engine that route ran on
stays (`core::amigainstall`) - BoingBags 3&4 and any Installer-script package still need
it - and `boingbags-39-3-4.json` is the recipe that still declares one.
The readings that block recorded are not lost: they are in this file's git history, in
ART-186, ART-193 and ART-227, and in `.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-amiga-side-install`.
_why_post_place: What the tree still needs once ART has placed this package's files: ten of them, for the
reason ART-227 records. (It used to have an Amiga-side twin, `amiga_installer.post_install`,
carrying the identical list for the emulator route; that route was removed on 2026-09-08
and this list is now the only one.) `Resident` refuses a command without the `p` bit, AmigaOS
3.9's own boot makes commands resident, and a tree missing these boots and then fails a
line at a time.
**Measured against the Updater's own tree, not copied from the list above.** The round-3
measurement hashed every file of a clean AmigaOS 3.9 tree and of the tree ART's own
BoingBag 1 emulator run produced (`E:\amiga\ProjeART\r3-measure\logs`, 2026-09-08). Of
the 4 015 files in the second, the `.uaem` sidecars that differ are exactly these ten
files' - `C/SetEnv.uaem` and `C/WBRun.uaem` created, `C/LoadMonDrvs.uaem`,
`C/LoadResource.uaem` and `C/wbinfo.uaem` changed from `----rwed` to `--p-rwed`,
`S/Startup-Sequence-BB3.9-1.uaem` and `S/Stream-Amplifier.rexx.uaem` created as `-s--rwed`
- and `C/MakeDir`, `C/MakeLink` and `S/Start-Amplifier.rexx` already carried the bit off
the CD, so setting it there is a no-op rather than a change. A host placement that copied
the payload and stopped would leave seven files differing from the Updater's tree, and
nothing would say so: exactly the failure that does not crash.
The same ten are what HstWB Installer sets, in the same two groups (`+prwed` on the
commands, `+srwed` on the scripts), which is where the list was found. Every one is placed
by this package's own payload, so `protect`'s refusal of an absent file cannot fire on a
placement that succeeded.
_why_chain_position: 2 of the material's own order (design section 1 of 2026-09-08-os-builder-chain-design.md): the CD is 1, and BoingBag 3.9-1 is the first thing that goes on it. Its own Install script reads version.library off the target and refuses anything but 45, which is the arrow the chain draws between rows 1 and 2.
